_comment: PROVENANCE RECORD for InvisiProxy. This file is the machine-readable answer to
'which upstream version is this integration built against, and what did we take
from it?'. It is data, not configuration — nothing at runtime reads it to decide
behaviour. docs/proxy/INVISIPROXY.md is the prose version and the upgrade procedure.
NOTE THE SHAPE OF THIS INTEGRATION: ZoFHub vendors NO InvisiProxy code. The
'incorporated' list below is empty on purpose, and 'adopted' records ideas that
were reimplemented from scratch against different libraries. See 'rationale'.
rationale: InvisiProxy is a complete web-proxy APPLICATION, not a library, and it is built on the same upstream primitives ZoFHub already integrates directly: Ultraviolet, Scramjet, Wisp, bare-mux, epoxy and libcurl. Vendoring it would duplicate working architecture rather than add capability.

It runs on Fastify 5 under a pnpm workspace; ZoFHub is Express 4 under npm with no build step. Its package.json also declares `postinstall: playwright install chromium`, which this repository's .npmrc (ignore-scripts=true) exists to prevent.

It is AGPL-3.0 and ZoFHub's own LICENSE is proprietary. ZoFHub serves over a network, so copying InvisiProxy source into the served work would engage AGPL-3.0 §13 for the resulting combination and oblige ZoFHub to offer its own corresponding source. Keeping it as a separately deployed service leaves those obligations with whoever deploys it.

adopted.idea: An explicit, application-level egress policy for the Wisp tunnel rather than reliance on library defaults.
adopted.upstreamReference: src/server.mjs — the Mrrowisp constructor (allowPrivateIPs: false, allowUDP: false, whitelist.ports, connectionsLimitPerIP, floodProtection)
adopted.note: Reimplemented against @mercuryworkshop/wisp-js's own option object. Upstream uses a different Wisp server (mrrowisp) with a different API, so no line of it is applicable, let alone copied. What was taken is the argument that these values belong in the application's configuration.

adopted.idea: A runnable check that every proxy engine actually serves pages.
adopted.note: Method deliberately NOT adopted. Upstream fetches the generated proxy URL with axios and asserts status 200; a service worker does not intercept requests from a client it does not control, so that request bypasses the proxy and reports the origin server's response. ZoFHub's version drives a real browser and asserts on the rendered document.

rejected.component: Fastify server, routes, templates, views and pages
rejected.reason: ZoFHub has its own Express application and its own site.

ZoFHub's wisp-js integration is pinned by test/wisp-egress-contract.test.mjs and carries proxied traffic through sing-box via an injected TCPSocket. Swapping the Wisp server would discard verified working architecture and that egress guarantee.

Upstream's own release note says 'may have issues not tested in-depth'. ZoFHub's npm 3.2.10 is verified working by tools/verify-proxy.mjs, so switching to an unpinnable GitHub tarball would replace a working dependency with an untested one. Recorded as the upgrade path if 'TypeError: headers is not iterable' is ever observed.
ZoFHub routes egress server-side through sing-box (docs/proxy/SINGBOX.md). Adding a second, browser-side proxy selector would be a duplicate mechanism with a weaker guarantee.
ZoFHub is configured by environment variables and validates them at startup.

deployment.runsIn: its own deployment, on the operator's infrastructure
